content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes to add global averaged pooled token value back to tokens for boosting vision transformers’ performance. It shows its motivation from learned attention maps of current ViT tend to have high entropy, thus the paper tries to add uniform attention, which has the highest entropy of attention map. Experiments are conducted on ImageNet classification and ADE20k segmentation to show its effectiveness.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength: 
1.	The paper interprets the high entropy of attention maps  
phenomenon from the optimization perspective, and motivates well to use its proposed uniform attention.
2.	The proposed method is simple and easy to integrate to existing method. 

Weaknesses:
1.	Interpretation of the high entropy of attention maps. Many existing works [1][2][3] indicate attention collapse problem / over-smoothing will hurt the performance of vision transformers, which is the opposite conclusion of this paper of ‘making the attention more uniform’, can authors discuss more about this? 
2.	Models not optimized well can also see smooth attention / softmax weights, which does not necessarily lead to uniform attention is good, can authors comment on that?
3.	The experiments results are somehow not convincing, mostly the CB block has improvement on small ViTs, e.g. ViT-Ti, for base size ViT, only very limited 0.1/0.2% ImageNet improvement. It remains questionable if the proposed method can be further scaled to applied to larger models, ViT-H, or other large ViT variants.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The clarity of this paper is good, novelty is limited, reproducibility is high as the proposed method is very simple.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall this paper introduces global average pooling, which is a common techniques of CNNs to vision transformers. The experiments results are not quite convincing and remain unknown if the method can still help with large models/well-optimized models.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This work studies the role of the density of the attention in Vision Transformer. It provides preliminary analyses that the spatial interactions of attention maps are close to dense interactions rather than sparse ones.  It thus manually inserts uniform attention to each layer of ViT models to supply the needed dense interactions. The proposed method Context Broadcasting, CB is applied after the MLP of ViT.  Experimental results are conducted on the vanilla ViT on image classification.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1. This work is well-written and easy to follow.
2. The proposed SE module is simple to implement.  

Weaknesses:
1. This work is not well-motivated and lacks novelty.  The claims that 'ViTs hungry for more spatial connections' is not well validated. 
2. The experiments to validate 'Are ViTs hungry for more spatial connections?' is unfair. Even the eight-layer ViT with additional MSA has about 0.15M lower parameters and 0.99M higher FLOPs than that of MLP, FLOPs have more effects than parameters in ViT. So it is predictable that the performance of MSA is slightly better than MLP in Fig2.
3. The proposed CB module achieves very marginal improvement, only based on the vanilla ViT. What about the performance improvement on advanced ViT like Swin[2], PVT[2], T2T-ViT[3], Cswin[4], etc.? 
4. SE also not works very well in ViT as discussed by T2T-ViT[3]. Taking SE as a comparison baseline is not a good choice.

[1] Liu, Ze, et al. "Swin transformer: Hierarchical vision transformer using shifted windows." Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision. 2021.
[2] Wang, Wenhai, et al. "Pyramid vision transformer: A versatile backbone for dense prediction without convolutions." Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision. 2021.
[3] Yuan, Li, et al. "Tokens-to-token vit: Training vision transformers from scratch on imagenet." Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision. 2021.
[4] Dong, Xiaoyi, et al. "Cswin transformer: A general vision transformer backbone with cross-shaped windows." Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition. 2022.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The overall work lacks novelty and does not reach the bar of the top-tire conference.  This work ensures reproducibility by attaching the 1 line code implementation.
content.summary_of_the_review: The overall work lacks novelty, and the proposed CB module is trivial.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper studies the role of the attention mechanism in vision transformers. Different from the previous works, the authors analyze the density of the attention and find out that the current ViTs tend to learn dense attention, which turns out to be hard to learn. To mitigate this problem, they propose to insert a new pooling layer to the ViT structure, which alleviate the learning burden of the self-attention layers for better performance.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1. The analysis about the density of the attention is simple yet insightful.

Problems:
1. I wonder if Fig.1(b) can be called as a dense attention since only about 16% tokens are referred to in the attention.
2. I think it would be better if the authors can add more details about the effect of context broadcasting in the introduction, or maybe it can be illustrated in the teaser figure.
3. I wonder if the same property of dense attention appears in all ViTs with different training technique. Is it possible that utilizing self-supervised methods to train the ViT can mitigate this problem?
4. The authors may have some discussion about the difference and advantage between their proposed method and directly regularizing the sparsity of self-attentions, which can lead to lower density.
5. It would be better if the authors can reorganize Fig.10. It is hard to see whether the attention is semantically meaningful with flattened tokens.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: This description in this paper is generally clear and easy to understand. The specific topic studied in this paper is quite novel and interesting, which I think can inspire many future works. The authors provide the code snippet in the appendix. Therefore it should be easy to reproduce the corresponding results in this paper.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper provides a good point for studying the effect of multi-head self-attention in ViTs, which can be helpful for better understanding how this architecture works for vision tasks.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper:
- The author designed an experiment to demonstrate ViT benefits from using dense interaction that models long-term dependences.
- This paper proposed a Context Broadcasting Module that imposes uniform attention on the current VIT modules.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Pros:
1. The CB and CBs are easy to implement.

Cons:
1. Experiment 1 (sec 2.1) designed an experiment to verify the effectiveness of dense interaction (Multi-head self-attention (MSA)). Although MSA shows better over MLPs, little has been discussed about why an 8-layer ViT is inserted in the front of a MSA or MLP. Not to mention other components such as Layer Normalization operation and residual connection.

2. The author discussed the steepest gradient problem without any qualitative examples. I found it hard to follow the claimed motivation in Experiment 3 (sec 2.1). In fact, can the steepest gradient solve by the LN in the following transformer layer?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The novelty of this paper is limited. 
- First, in terms of dense interactions, the paper provided limited analysis on MSA/MLP and lacked discussion on other components in Transformer. 
- Second, the paper identifies the steepest gradient. However, little has been discussed about whether the problem is solved by normalization techniques already applied in Transformer. 
- Third, no motivation or analysis is discussed to support the formulation of the CB module (equation 1).

Besides technique novelty, I found the experiment `WHERE TO INSERT CB IN A VIT` confusing. Since this section only offers experiments but no discussion on why inserting CBS at the end of MLPs can yield better results.
content.summary_of_the_review: Considering the weaknesses discussed above, I would like to reject this paper. This paper needs more detailed analysis to motivate and support the contribution.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 1: The contributions are neither significant nor novel.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper studies the density of attention maps in MSA of ViT. The paper uses empirical studies and theoretical analysis shows the transformer prefers spatial interaction, and dense attention maps and the gradient of dense attention maps is unstable. The paper proposes to add CB/CBs module that relaxes the dense interaction. Experiments show that, with a minor FLOPs increase, the model outperforms the previous method in both classification and segmentation tasks.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
+ The paper proposes an effective block that improves the Vision Transformer backbone, with minimum FLOPs increment.

+ The paper provides a thorough evaluation of the 'density' of attention maps and reveals how the CB changes the 'density' of attention maps. 

Weakness:
+ The paper didn't provide an empirical study on how the gradient changes while the 'density' of attention changes. This can be analyzed by collecting the density as well as the gradient at different layers while training the ViT.
+ The paper didn't provide results on the Object Detection task as SE did. 
+ The paper didn't provide the generalizability of this module on other transformer-based models, for example, PVT, and SWIN Transformers.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is well-written and high-quality paper. The empirical study is novel. The method is easy to reproduce.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper provides a thorough analysis of the attention density of ViT. It provides a useful module for image classification and segmentation tasks. However, the paper fails the show the compatibility of this block with other transformer-based backbones. I'm willing to raise my score if the author can address my concern during the rebuttal.
